“The Malian military, armed groups and insurgent forces are committing grave laws-of-war violations while international organizations and governments largely stand by,” the rights watchdog said in its report, urging the African Union’s Peace and Security Council to take action.
The latest report was based on interviews with 30 people conducted between July 30 and Sept. 20, including journalists, rights activists, community leaders and a Malian soldier.
HRW identified “two apparently indiscriminate Malian military drone attacks,” one of which partly destroyed a health facility in the country’s north in July, while another hit a market in August, killing “six civilians” and injuring “at least 20 others.”
